arabic_grammar_name: ma masdariyya vs ma mawsula: the resumptive-pronoun and masdar-substitution tests
plain_rule: Ma masdariyya converts a following verb clause into the equivalent of a verbal noun and never takes a resumptive pronoun referring back to it; ma mawsula (relative) always needs one, or itself fills a gap left by the following verb's missing argument. Certain preceding particles (ba'da, qabla) categorically force the masdariyya reading regardless of the following clause. Ma masdariyya is mabni and carries no visible case of its own; when its clause is the second term of a construct it occupies only the position of the genitive. A relative ma-clause heading a sentence makes that whole sentence nominal, with the clause itself as subject -- and endings can only be assigned after that structure, never before, is parsed.
trigger_condition: a ma-plus-verb clause's function (masdariyya vs relative) or its case/sentence-type consequences are being decided without first checking for a resumptive pronoun, a categorical particle restriction, or the clause's own sentence-initial role
expected_feature: masdariyya read from the absence of a resumptive pronoun or a categorical particle restriction (ba'da/qabla), a masdariyya clause as construct second term left with no visible case (positional genitive only), and a relative ma-clause correctly read as the subject of a nominal sentence before any ending is assigned
typical_error_feature: a relative reading defaulted to on frequency alone despite no resumptive pronoun, a categorical particle restriction ignored, a nominative ending invented for a mabni masdariyya clause, a relative-headed sentence misclassified as verbal, or endings vocalised before the sentence is parsed
point_template: Check for a resumptive pronoun and any preceding particle restriction before deciding whether this ma is masdariyya or relative.
teach_template: Ma masdariyya has no resumptive pronoun and is mabni; ma mawsula needs (or fills) one and heads a nominal sentence as its subject. Some particles force the masdariyya reading outright, and every ending follows the parsed structure, never precedes it.
bottom_out_template: State whether a resumptive pronoun is present, name any particle restriction, and give the case/sentence-type consequence.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner defaults a ma-plus-verb clause to the relative reading because it is more familiar, without checking whether the following verb carries a resumptive pronoun.
A learner assigns a visible case ending to a mabni masdariyya-ma clause instead of recognising it occupies only a positional case.

arabic_grammar_name: ma al-hijaziyya (laysa-like government) and the structural triggers that cancel it
plain_rule: Ma can govern a nominal sentence like laysa (ism marfu', khabar mansub) only under conditions; several structural triggers cancel that government outright, returning both terms to plain nominative agreement: an intervening illa that turns the negation into a restriction, fronting the predicate before the subject, and fronting a complement of the predicate before the subject (though that fronted complement keeps its own separate case). A correction with bal opens a fresh, independently-cased predication rather than continuing the original government, and a preceding interrogative hamza converts the whole particle into a rhetorical question with no laysa-like government at all.
trigger_condition: a ma-headed nominal sentence's case pattern is being assigned as if the laysa-like government always applies, without checking for illa-breaking, predicate fronting, fronted-complement, a following bal-correction, or a preceding interrogative hamza
expected_feature: the laysa-like government correctly cancelled (both terms nominative) whenever one of its named triggers is present, and correctly applied (ism marfu', khabar mansub) only when none of them is
typical_error_feature: the accusative predicate kept after illa breaks the negation, after the predicate or its complement is fronted, across a bal-correction, or after a preceding interrogative hamza removes the negation reading entirely
point_template: Check for illa, predicate/complement fronting, a following bal, or a preceding interrogative hamza before assigning ma's laysa-like government.
teach_template: Ma's laysa-like government (ism marfu', khabar mansub) is conditional, not automatic: illa-breaking, predicate or complement fronting, a following bal-correction, or a preceding interrogative hamza each cancel or bypass it, returning the sentence to plain nominative agreement.
bottom_out_template: Name which trigger (if any) is present and state the resulting case of both terms.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner keeps a ma-headed predicate accusative after illa has broken the negation into a restriction, instead of recognising the government is cancelled.
A learner keeps ma's laysa-like government after a preceding interrogative hamza has converted the particle into a rhetorical question with no negation at all.

arabic_grammar_name: amma as in fused with ma kaffa, and its obligatory jawab-fa
plain_rule: Amma is historically the conditional particle in fused with a preventive ma that neutralizes in's own government, together presupposing an unstated general condition; it is not an ordinary coordinator. Because its own government is neutralized, its apodosis cannot attach directly the way a plain subject attaches to a plain predicate, so the jawab-fa is obligatory before the apodosis in every shape -- nominal, future-marked, imperative, or terse -- and it carries a structurally required resultative link that a plain coordinating wa, or the apparent economy of an English translation, does not license dropping.
trigger_condition: an amma clause's link to its apodosis, or the presence/absence of the following fa, is being decided as if amma were an ordinary coordinator or as if the fa were an optional stylistic addition
expected_feature: amma read as a conditional-like particle presupposing an unstated general condition, with the jawab-fa treated as obligatory before its apodosis in every shape, and never conflated with the plain coordinating wa or dropped on the grounds of an English translation's economy
typical_error_feature: amma treated as a plain coordinator expecting a second coordinand, the jawab-fa omitted before a nominal, future-marked, imperative, or terse apodosis, or the jawab-fa treated as interchangeable with wa or as an optional translation artifact
point_template: Check that amma's apodosis is linked by the obligatory jawab-fa, whatever shape the apodosis takes.
teach_template: Amma is a fused conditional-like particle whose own government is neutralized, so its apodosis needs the jawab-fa to attach at all; that fa is not a coordinator and not optional, regardless of the apodosis's shape or how the sentence is translated.
bottom_out_template: State that amma presupposes an unstated condition and that the jawab-fa is obligatory before its apodosis.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner treats amma as an ordinary coordinator and expects a second coordinand after the following fa, instead of recognising the fa as an obligatory jawab-fa.
A learner omits the jawab-fa before amma's apodosis because a terse English translation needs no equivalent linking word.

arabic_grammar_name: ma ta'ajjubiyya (exclamatory) vs the interrogative elative predicate, and their opposite case patterns
plain_rule: The same af'al-shaped skeleton licenses two structurally different constructions: exclamatory ma plus a frozen ta'ajjub verb, whose object is always accusative and whose verb never agrees in number or gender with that object; and an ordinary interrogative elative noun annexed to a genitive complement, whose complement is always genitive, never accusative. The answer-expectation test -- does the utterance expect an answer, or express astonishment with none expected -- must run before either case pattern is applied.
trigger_condition: a noun or verb-form following an af'al-shaped word is being cased, or agreement is being assigned to that word, without first running the answer-expectation test to choose between the exclamatory and interrogative constructions
expected_feature: the accusative object and invariant frozen-verb agreement of the exclamatory reading, and the genitive muda ilayh of the interrogative-elative reading, each applied only after the answer-expectation test selects the right construction
typical_error_feature: a genitive specifier supplied for the exclamatory frozen verb's accusative object, an accusative object supplied for the interrogative elative's genitive complement, or the frozen verb wrongly inflected to agree with its object
point_template: Run the answer-expectation test before assigning case to the word following an af'al-shaped skeleton.
teach_template: Exclamatory ma's frozen verb takes an invariant accusative object; the interrogative elative predicate takes a genitive muda ilayh. The same skeleton licenses both, so the answer-expectation test, not the skeleton, decides the case pattern.
bottom_out_template: State which reading (exclamatory or interrogative) the test selects and give the resulting case.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner marks the object of a frozen ta'ajjub verb genitive, as if ma were interrogative governing an annexed specifier.
A learner adds a feminine ending to a frozen ta'ajjub verb to agree with a feminine object, breaking its required invariance.

arabic_grammar_name: ma laka an + subjunctive: the denial-of-entitlement frame and its lam
plain_rule: Ma plus a kasra-vowelled possessive/entitlement lam plus an together form one frame denying a right or entitlement ("you have no right to..."), not plain negation of an action; an inside this frame governs the following verb into the subjunctive. A bare command-lam without an is a different frame entirely, governing the jussive directly. And the vowel on the lam proclitic itself is load-bearing: a fatha selects the unrelated emphatic lam, which is incompatible with ma's negation.
trigger_condition: a ma-laka-an clause's overall sense, its verb's mood, or the vowel on its lam proclitic is being decided without recognising the whole ma-laka-an sequence as one denial-of-entitlement frame
expected_feature: ma-laka-an read as a single denial-of-entitlement frame, its verb correctly put in the subjunctive under an, a bare command-lam recognised as a separate jussive-governing frame, and the lam proclitic correctly vowelled with kasra for the possessive/entitlement reading
typical_error_feature: the frame read as plain negation of a completed action, the verb after an left indicative, the command-lam's jussive conflated with the an-frame's subjunctive, or the lam proclitic wrongly vowelled with fatha
point_template: Read ma-laka-an as one denial-of-entitlement frame before assigning a mood or a vowel to any of its pieces.
teach_template: Ma plus a kasra-vowelled lam plus an together deny a right, not an action; an governs the subjunctive, a bare command-lam without an governs the jussive instead, and a fatha on the lam selects an unrelated, incompatible emphatic particle.
bottom_out_template: Name the frame's governor (an or the bare command-lam) and state the resulting mood and the lam's correct vowel.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner reads ma laka an tafala as plain negation of a completed action, ignoring that laka an together deny a right or entitlement.
A learner leaves the verb after an indicative instead of putting it in the subjunctive that an governs.

arabic_grammar_name: lamma al-jazima (not yet, jussive-governing) vs the unrelated non-governing temporal lamma
plain_rule: The written form lamma covers two rival particles: lamma al-jazima, which governs the jussive on a following mudari' exactly as lam does (deleting a weak final letter or a final nun for its exponent, and marking a sound verb with sukun, never fatha), and the unrelated non-governing temporal lamma ("when"). Confusing the two, or borrowing the subjunctive's exponent for the jazm-governing one, misreads which particle -- and which government, if any -- is actually present.
trigger_condition: a verb following the written form lamma is being vowelled, or its final letter/nun is being kept or dropped, without first deciding whether this occurrence is the jussive-governing lamma al-jazima or the unrelated non-governing temporal lamma
expected_feature: lamma al-jazima's jussive government correctly realized through weak-letter deletion, nun-deletion, or sukun as the verb class requires, and never conflated with the non-governing temporal lamma's lack of any such government
typical_error_feature: a weak final letter or final nun retained under lamma al-jazima as though it were non-governing, a subjunctive fatha substituted for the jussive's sukun, or lamma al-jazima's fixed past/elapsed reference paired with a future adverbial
point_template: Decide which lamma this is -- jussive-governing or non-governing temporal -- before vowelling the following verb.
teach_template: Lamma al-jazima governs the jussive exactly like lam, with the same weak-letter/nun-deletion or sukun exponents, and fixes past/elapsed reference; the unrelated temporal lamma governs nothing. The two must never be treated as interchangeable or as sharing one exponent.
bottom_out_template: State which lamma is present and give the resulting exponent on the following verb.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner keeps a weak final letter or a final nun under lamma al-jazima's government, as though lamma here were the unrelated non-governing temporal particle.
A learner marks a sound verb under lamma al-jazima with the subjunctive's fatha instead of the jussive's sukun.

arabic_grammar_name: ma zala / baraha / fati'a / infakka: the negative-only kana-sisters and their government
plain_rule: Ma zala/baraha/fati'a/infakka form a continuous-negation kana-sister family: the ma fused into the idiom is a negative-polarity licenser, not the separate jussive-governing lam, so the present-tense form of the idiom (ma yazalu) stays indicative. The family is already inherently negative and does not take a further stacked negator from an unrelated system such as lan. Like kana, it assigns its ism the nominative and its khabar the accusative; that khabar may be nominal or a mudari' clause depicting a continuing state, but the idiom can never mean simple negation of a single completed action.
trigger_condition: a ma-zala-family verb's mood, its need for a further negator, its ism/khabar case, or its meaning is being decided without treating the whole family as one negative-only kana-sister construction
expected_feature: the present-tense form of the idiom left indicative, no additional negator stacked onto it, its ism marked nominative and khabar accusative, and its meaning read as continuing state/action rather than single-event negation
typical_error_feature: the present-tense form wrongly put in the jussive as though ma governed it like lam, a further negator such as lan stacked onto it, its khabar wrongly marked nominative, or the idiom used to mean simple negation of a single completed action
point_template: Treat ma zala and its sisters as one negative-only kana-sister family before assigning mood, a further negator, or a case.
teach_template: Ma zala's own ma is a negative-polarity licenser, not a jussive governor, so the present-tense form stays indicative; the family is already negative and takes no further negator; and it governs ism-marfu'/khabar-mansub like kana while meaning continuing state, never single-event negation.
bottom_out_template: State the family's own government (ism/khabar case) and its continuing-state meaning.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner puts ma yazalu's verb in the jussive because ma superficially resembles the jussive-governing lam.
A learner marks ma zala's khabar nominative, as though the family were a non-governing adverbial phrase rather than a kana-sister.

arabic_grammar_name: ma dama: the fossilized durative-limit frame whose ma is never negation
plain_rule: Ma dama is a fossilized temporal-masdariyya frame ("as long as ... lasts") built on the durative kana-sister verb dama; despite its identical surface to the negator ma, the ma inside this frame contributes no negation whatsoever, and reading it as negation reverses the whole sentence's sense. The frame keeps dama in the perfect tense, with no jussive-governing negation and no mood question of the kind a prohibition would raise, and its khabar is an ordinary declinable accusative noun keeping its full nunation, never the bare no-nunation treatment that belongs only to a noun negated by the categorical negator la.
trigger_condition: a ma dama clause's meaning, its verb's tense/mood, or its khabar's nunation is being decided by treating this ma as an ordinary negator instead of recognising the fossilized durative-limit frame
expected_feature: ma dama read with no negation contributed by ma at all, dama kept in the perfect with no jussive/mood question raised, and its khabar treated as an ordinary declinable accusative noun keeping its tanween
typical_error_feature: the clause read as negated (reversing its sense), dama wrongly given a jussive-looking present form as though under a prohibition, or its khabar wrongly stripped of tanween as though it were la's own bare negated noun
point_template: Recognise ma dama as a fossilized durative-limit frame before reading any negation, mood, or nunation off its surface resemblance to other ma/la constructions.
teach_template: Ma dama's ma contributes no negation; dama stays perfect with no mood question, and its khabar is an ordinary accusative noun with full tanween -- none of the negation-family rules that look similar on the surface apply inside this frame.
bottom_out_template: State that ma contributes no negation here and give dama's tense and the khabar's case/nunation.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner reads a ma dama clause as negated, reversing its sense, because ma superficially resembles the ordinary negator.
A learner strips the tanween from ma dama's khabar as though it were the bare noun negated by the categorical negator la.

arabic_grammar_name: ma al-nafiya: plain statement negation with no mood government at all
plain_rule: Plain ma negates a statement without carrying prohibitive force and without governing the following mudari' into any dependent mood; a verb negated by ma keeps its own indicative ending regardless. This is unlike la, which can govern the jussive in its prohibitive use, and unlike lam, which specifically shifts a present-form verb's reference to past time under its own jussive government. The negator must be chosen by the intended time reference and function, not by which one is more familiar.
trigger_condition: a verb negated by ma is being assigned a jussive ending, or ma is being treated as carrying prohibitive force, or lam is being substituted for ma out of familiarity rather than the intended time reference
expected_feature: a verb negated by plain ma kept indicative, ma never read as prohibitive, and the negator (ma vs lam vs la) chosen by its actual function and time reference
typical_error_feature: a jussive ending assigned to a verb negated by plain ma, ma read as though it carried la's prohibitive force, or lam substituted for present-time negation out of familiarity, shifting the meaning to a completed past event
point_template: Check whether the negator actually governs mood (lam, or la in its prohibitive use) before assigning any ending to the verb it negates.
teach_template: Plain ma has no mood effect at all and never carries prohibitive force; a verb it negates keeps its indicative ending. Choose the negator (ma/lam/la) by its actual function and the intended time reference, not by which is most familiar.
bottom_out_template: Name the negator's actual function and give the resulting mood/time reference.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner puts a verb negated by plain ma into the jussive, as though ma governed mood the way lam does.
A learner substitutes lam for present-time negation out of familiarity, unintentionally shifting the sentence's meaning to a completed past event.

arabic_grammar_name: interrogative ma's obligatory alif-elision when directly governed by a preposition
plain_rule: Ma al-istifhamiyya drops its alif when a preposition governs it directly, giving the closed inventory lima, amma, mimma, fima, bima; when the preposition is min, its own final nun additionally assimilates into the mim, producing the geminated mimma rather than a separately spelled min ma. Keeping the alif in this position, or spelling the two words apart, does not just look different: it signals a different, non-interrogative function of ma, or is simply not a form the interrogative takes. This elision is specific to the interrogative reading and specific to each fused cluster; it is never generalized to an unrelated particle such as lamma that happens to share some of the same letters.
trigger_condition: a preposition-plus-ma sequence's spelling (alif retained or dropped, fused or written apart) is being decided without checking whether ma here is interrogative and without checking which specific fused cluster the preposition selects
expected_feature: the alif dropped and, for min, the nun assimilated into the mim, whenever a preposition directly governs interrogative ma, and the correct fused cluster used for each preposition rather than a separately spelled or unrelated form
typical_error_feature: the alif kept after a directly-governing preposition, the preposition and ma spelled apart instead of fused, or the interrogative cluster confused with an unrelated particle that happens to share some of the same letters
point_template: Check whether this is interrogative ma directly governed by a preposition before deciding whether to drop the alif and how to fuse the cluster.
teach_template: Interrogative ma drops its alif under a directly-governing preposition, and min's own nun assimilates into the mim (mimma); each fused cluster is a specific, closed form, never optional spelling and never confusable with an unrelated particle.
bottom_out_template: Name the fused interrogative cluster the preposition selects and state why the alif is dropped.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner keeps the alif on interrogative ma after a directly-governing preposition, writing لِمَا for 'why' instead of لِمَ.
A learner spells min and interrogative ma as two separate words instead of the required fused, geminated form mimma.

arabic_grammar_name: relative/masdariyya ma after a preposition: retained alif, positional genitive, and lexically fixed prepositions
plain_rule: Relative and masdariyya ma keep their alif when governed by a preposition (bima, mimma, fima), unlike the interrogative's alif-elision, which does not generalize to this function. A verb's preposition-plus-ma pairing can be a fixed lexical selection, not a free choice among prepositions that seem semantically similar in English. And two prepositions that both translate loosely are still not interchangeable: mimma (min) introduces a source or starting point, while fima (fi) introduces the topic or subject matter a discussion or feeling concerns; swapping them changes what the clause claims.
trigger_condition: a preposition-plus-ma sequence's spelling, its choice of preposition, or the sense that preposition contributes is being decided without checking that this ma is relative/masdariyya (not interrogative), without checking the governing verb's own lexical preposition, or without checking whether source/origin or topic/subject-matter is actually meant
expected_feature: the alif kept on relative/masdariyya ma after a preposition, the verb's own lexically fixed preposition used rather than a semantically-plausible substitute, and mimma vs fima chosen correctly by source/origin vs topic/subject-matter
typical_error_feature: the interrogative's alif-elision rule wrongly applied to a relative/masdariyya ma, a semantically-plausible-but-lexically-wrong preposition substituted for a verb's fixed partner, or mimma and fima swapped for one another
point_template: Check that this ma is relative/masdariyya (keeping its alif) and that its preposition is the verb's own lexical partner and the right sense (source vs topic).
teach_template: Relative/masdariyya ma keeps its alif after a preposition; some verbs are lexically bound to one particular preposition regardless of general meaning; and mimma (source) and fima (topic) are not interchangeable even though both can be rendered loosely in English.
bottom_out_template: State that the alif is kept, name the verb's lexically fixed preposition (if any), and give the source-vs-topic sense.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner drops the alif on relative ma after a preposition, wrongly applying the interrogative's alif-elision rule to a different function of ma.
A learner pairs a verb with whichever preposition sounds semantically plausible instead of the one that verb lexically selects.

arabic_grammar_name: ma's clause-initial scope, its default singular-masculine agreement, and the ma-vs-man rational/non-rational split
plain_rule: As an interrogative operator, ma must sit at the front of its clause, scoping rightward over everything that follows; moved elsewhere it leaves the clause with no question operator in scope. As a relative/conditional pronoun, ma controls default singular-masculine agreement on the verb referring to it, regardless of the notional plurality of what it refers to. And ma itself is reserved for non-rational referents ("what"); asking about a person's identity requires the rational interrogative man ("who") instead.
trigger_condition: ma's clause position, the agreement of a verb referring back to ma, or the choice between ma and man is being decided without checking clause-initial position, default singular-masculine agreement, or the rational status of the referent
expected_feature: ma kept clause-initial as an interrogative operator, default singular-masculine agreement kept on a verb referring to ma regardless of notional plurality, and man used instead of ma whenever the referent is a rational (human) one
typical_error_feature: ma moved out of clause-initial position, a verb referring to ma wrongly pluralized to match notional plurality, or ma used to ask about a person instead of man
point_template: Check ma's clause position, its default agreement, and the referent's rational status before finalizing the sentence.
teach_template: Ma as a question operator must be clause-initial; as a relative/conditional pronoun it controls default singular-masculine agreement regardless of real-world plurality; and ma itself is reserved for non-rational referents, with man reserved for people.
bottom_out_template: State ma's required clause position, its default agreement, or why man (not ma) is needed here.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner moves interrogative ma out of clause-initial position, leaving the clause with no question operator in scope.
A learner uses non-rational ma to ask about a person instead of the rational interrogative man.

arabic_grammar_name: innama: inna neutralized by ma kaffa into a last-element restriction particle
plain_rule: Innama is inna fused with a preventive ma that neutralizes inna's own case government entirely, returning both terms to plain nominative agreement, while together the fused particle contributes a restriction ("only") that plain inna does not carry. The restriction's exclusion always falls on whichever element is mentioned LAST in the clause, not the first. Plain inna and innama are not interchangeable: only innama carries the restriction meaning, and only plain inna carries the ism-accusative/khabar-nominative government.
trigger_condition: an innama clause's restriction target, or a choice between plain inna and innama, is being decided without checking which element is mentioned last or without checking whether the restriction meaning and the case government are being kept consistent with the same particle
expected_feature: the restriction correctly targeted at the last-mentioned element, and plain inna (government, no restriction) kept distinct from innama (no government, restriction)
typical_error_feature: the restriction wrongly targeted at the first-mentioned element, or plain inna and innama used interchangeably, borrowing one particle's meaning with the other's case pattern
point_template: Identify the last-mentioned element as innama's restriction target, and keep plain inna's government separate from innama's restriction.
teach_template: Innama's ma kaffa cancels inna's government and adds a restriction that targets whichever element is named last; plain inna keeps its government but has no restriction sense. The two are never interchangeable.
bottom_out_template: Name the last-mentioned element as the restriction's target, and state which particle (inna or innama) the sentence actually needs.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner reads innama's restriction as targeting the first-mentioned element instead of the last-mentioned one.
A learner uses plain inna's case government while intending innama's restriction meaning, producing an inconsistent sentence.

arabic_grammar_name: lamma al-jazima's requirement of a mudari' verb, never a perfect-form verb
plain_rule: Lamma al-jazima, like lam, only ever governs a mudari' (present-form) verb; the past-to-present "not yet" meaning comes from the particle's own jussive government acting on that present-form verb, never from pairing the particle with a perfect-form verb the way a plain time adverb might. Pairing lamma al-jazima with a perfect-form verb is ungrammatical, not merely stylistically unusual.
trigger_condition: a clause combining lamma al-jazima with a following verb is being formed without checking whether that verb is in the mudari' (present) form the particle's own government requires
expected_feature: lamma al-jazima always paired with a mudari' verb, whose jussive-marked form itself supplies the past-to-present 'not yet' reading
typical_error_feature: lamma al-jazima paired with a perfect-form verb, treating the particle as a plain time adverb rather than a governor that requires its own present-form target
point_template: Check that the verb following lamma al-jazima is in the mudari' form before finalizing the sentence.
teach_template: Lamma al-jazima's own jussive government on a mudari' verb is what supplies the 'not yet' meaning; it can never be paired with a perfect-form verb instead.
bottom_out_template: Confirm the verb after lamma al-jazima is mudari' and state how its government supplies the 'not yet' meaning.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner pairs lamma al-jazima with a perfect-form verb, treating the particle as a plain time adverb instead of a governor requiring a mudari' verb.
